Subject: Stray Instances of Dishonour of Cheques 
This is in continuation of OM No. No. Bkg.1(5)2006/Banking Agreement/Part./ dated 12.04.2010 
on the subject cited above. 
The issue of dishonor of cheques was raised with Dy. Managing Director, State Bank of India vide 
DO No. Bkg.12)2006/NFMS/Vol.III dated 15.04.2010. In this connection, CGM(SME), SBI, Corporate 
Centre has instructed Chief General Manager of the Circle to advise all the link branches for EPFO to 
urgently review the position of EPFO accounts pertaining to Account No.1 and Account No.10 at the

NEW FUND MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (NFMS)  
DISHONOUR OF EPFO CHEQUS BY BRANCHES 
Please refer to our letter No. 135 dated 28.01.2006 and subsequent Setters 
regarding NFMS. 
2. Under the arrangement, it has been advised to fix up necessary overdrawing 
limits in current accounts of EPFO, at link branches, pertaining to EPFO a/c no 1 
and 10 so that the cheques drawn by EF'FO on the accounts will be paid at any 
center. The balance in the accounts whether in debit or credit is to be transferred 
to Mumbai Main Branch (MMB) through auto-sweeps so that the day end balance. in 
the accounts is made To zero. Necessary limits are sanctioned against fixed 
deposits at MMB to take care of the overdraft, if any at MMB taking into account the 
overall transfer of debit/credit balances from link branches. 
Further as per 
arrangement, we have to pay penal interest for the balances not transferred to MMB 
on the same day. 
3. Of late, we are receiving regular complaints from various EPFO Regional/Sub 
Regional offices(RO/SRO) that the cheques issued by EPFO are being returned 
stating the reason 'Insufficient funds which is creating severe problems for EPFO. 
The Central Provident Fund CoMmissiorrN has written a DO letter to DMD (NBG) 
expressing his grave concern on the issue of such returns highlighting that dishonor 
of cheques tarnishes the image of EPFO and causes hardship to .EPF0 subscribers 
entailing financial losses.
